But ultimately, it shows the strength of love and hope to overcome shared traumas that Indigenous peoples from Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific have continued to face.

When the train resumes, Iris suffers a bout of unconsciousness and wakes to find the old woman has disappeared. The other passengers ominously deny Miss Froy ever existed, so Iris begins to investigate with another traveller (Michael Redgrave) and, as the pair sleuth, romantic sparks fly.

In return Cheng helps her in the kitchen, surprising the locals with the delights of Chinese cuisine.

Stars Peter Cummins, David Gulpilil and Greg Rowe.

programme.title: Whale Rider

programme.title: We Are Still Here
programme.desc: We Are Still Here is a unique Indigenous film that interweaves eight powerful tales to tell a sweeping story of hope and survival. Through the eyes of eight protagonists, We Are Still Here traverses 1000 years from past, present, and future to explore stories of kinship, loss, grief, and resilience. But ultimately, it shows the strength of love and hope to overcome shared traumas that Indigenous peoples from Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific have continued to face.

programme.sub-title: Thessaloniki: Greece's De Facto Food City
programme.desc: In Thessaloniki, Diane explores the many influences that have shaped its unique cuisine. Along the way she learns the secrets of bougatsa, an airy, creamy phyllo pastry, with a master baker.

programme.title: Food Safari Earth
programme.desc: Maeve O'Meara returns with Food Safari Earth, exploring how multicultural Australia cooks with the delicious variety of fresh vegetables, fruits, herbs, grains, pulses and flowers cultivated by Mother Nature. Maeve meets Sydney chef Peter Gilmore, Thai chef Amy Chanta, Middle Eastern chef Joseph Abboud, and one of Australia's most acclaimed chefs, Martin Benn as they celebrate the awesome power of the humble vegetable across the world's cuisines.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: Capri embarks on the Skagit River with a member of the Upper Skagit tribe, a people who have lived off the seasonal salmon runs for thousands of years.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet: French Edition
programme.desc: Coming up today, Gabriel Gate brings us the flavors of Marseille with his Simple Bouillabaisse, the iconic fisherman's stew of the Mediterranean.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: Bushfood legend Rayleen Brown and stand-up sensation Andy Saunders join host Nornie Bero for a NAIDOC Week afternoon tea celebration.

programme.title: Instant Italian
programme.desc: Anna is transporting us to the Amalfi Coast in this lemon-themed episode where she shows us how to make a flavorful Chicken Piccata Stir Fry and a refreshing Limoncello Sorbet.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers Usa
programme.desc: The bikers are in Maine, where seafood is a way of life. They hop aboard the boat of a lifelong lobsterman, who literally shows them the ropes as they put in a day's work hauling in the tasty crustaceans. Back on land, the boys go digging for clams in muddy flats, and throw down a traditional beachfront seafood bake with a local chef.

programme.title: Ainsley's Football Feast
programme.desc: Ainsley Harriott rustles up a World Cup feast for footballer and presenter Jermaine Jenas and actress and presenter Denise Van Outen, while Candice Brown and Carl Anthony Brown will be helping.

programme.title: Come Dine With Me The Professionals
programme.desc: Today's Nottingham show kicks off at The Plough, where front of house manager Becky and chef Mark are aiming to showcase their gastro pub grub.

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: What does a chef eat when he's at home? For Victor it's claypot rice. It's a one-pot dish that’s soft, crispy, chewy and savoury all-in-one. Victor talks through which claypot is best to use, and how you can achieve fluffy rice plus a crispy bottom layer without burning.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: Bushfood legend Rayleen Brown and stand-up sensation Andy Saunders join host Nornie Bero for a NAIDOC Week afternoon tea celebration.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.desc: The Minas region of Brazil produces as much raw milk cheese as France, but most of it is illegal. Will takes a flight to the stunning Canastra ranges to learn about the traditional farm cheese and Pain de Quejo before heading further south to the remote Campos Altos region to discover a unique cheese made from the milk long horn cattle, and enjoys a traditional BBQ before returning to Sao Paulo for a lesson in grilling Coalho cheese.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers Comfort Food
programme.desc: Si and Dave cook dishes to feed a multitude - just the thing to impress your guests or to fill up the family. Their salmon pie with spinach and hollandaise is a showstopper and their chocolate and cherry buns make a perfect centrepiece.

programme.title: Kate And Larapinta
programme.desc: Kate Leeming embarks on a 700km solo cycle along Australia's remote Finke River. Battling searing heat, mechanical failures and exhaustion, she confronts physical limits and inner ghosts, turning her epic journey into a meditation on purpose, resilience, and what it takes to keep going.

programme.title: It Takes A Village
programme.desc: This documentary shines a light on a very different way of caring for people living with dementia. Korongee, a new facility in a northern suburb of Hobart, combines the world's best dementia care practices with new and revolutionary ideas. Including a focus on individuals and their life experiences, as the basis for their care. Korongee's guiding philosophy is that a person living with dementia is an individual with a rich and unique personality.

programme.desc: This heart-warming documentary follow the journey of former students in Dandenong North Primary School who came back to become teachers. To ‘give back’ and make a difference to the next generations, while welcoming all children and families with open arms.

programme.title: Storm Boy

programme.desc: We Are Still Here is a unique Indigenous film that interweaves eight powerful tales to tell a sweeping story of hope and survival. Through the eyes of eight protagonists, We Are Still Here traverses 1000 years from past, present, and future to explore stories of kinship, loss, grief, and resilience. But ultimately, it shows the strength of love and hope to overcome shared traumas that Indigenous peoples from Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific have continued to face.

programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Fruit can find its way onto any Italian table. Lidia starts with a refreshing eye-catching salad of shrimp and sweet melon dressed with a bright minty pesto.

programme.title: My Greek Table With Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: Diane explores the street food scene of Athens and is inspired to create some of her own gyro-stuffed baked bread, and a green bean salad with hazelnuts.

programme.title: My Greek Table With Diane Kochilas
programme.sub-title: Thessaloniki: Greece's De Facto Food City
programme.desc: In Thessaloniki, Diane explores the many influences that have shaped its unique cuisine. Along the way she learns the secrets of bougatsa, an airy, creamy phyllo pastry, with a master baker.

programme.title: Food Safari Earth
programme.desc: Maeve O'Meara returns with Food Safari Earth, exploring how multicultural Australia cooks with the delicious variety of fresh vegetables, fruits, herbs, grains, pulses and flowers cultivated by Mother Nature. Maeve meets Sydney chef Peter Gilmore, Thai chef Amy Chanta, Middle Eastern chef Joseph Abboud, and one of Australia's most acclaimed chefs, Martin Benn as they celebrate the awesome power of the humble vegetable across the world's cuisines.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: Capri embarks on the Skagit River with a member of the Upper Skagit tribe, a people who have lived off the seasonal salmon runs for thousands of years.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet: French Edition

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw

programme.title: Instant Italian
programme.desc: Anna is transporting us to the Amalfi Coast in this lemon-themed episode where she shows us how to make a flavorful Chicken Piccata Stir Fry and a refreshing Limoncello Sorbet.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers Usa
programme.desc: The bikers are in Maine, where seafood is a way of life. They hop aboard the boat of a lifelong lobsterman, who literally shows them the ropes as they put in a day's work hauling in the tasty crustaceans. Back on land, the boys go digging for clams in muddy flats, and throw down a traditional beachfront seafood bake with a local chef.

programme.title: Ainsley's Football Feast
programme.desc: Ainsley Harriott rustles up a World Cup feast for footballer and presenter Jermaine Jenas and actress and presenter Denise Van Outen, while Candice Brown and Carl Anthony Brown will be helping.

programme.title: Come Dine With Me The Professionals
programme.desc: Today's Nottingham show kicks off at The Plough, where front of house manager Becky and chef Mark are aiming to showcase their gastro pub grub.

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: What does a chef eat when he's at home? For Victor it's claypot rice. It's a one-pot dish that’s soft, crispy, chewy and savoury all-in-one. Victor talks through which claypot is best to use, and how you can achieve fluffy rice plus a crispy bottom layer without burning.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.desc: The Minas region of Brazil produces as much raw milk cheese as France, but most of it is illegal. Will takes a flight to the stunning Canastra ranges to learn about the traditional farm cheese and Pain de Quejo before heading further south to the remote Campos Altos region to discover a unique cheese made from the milk long horn cattle, and enjoys a traditional BBQ before returning to Sao Paulo for a lesson in grilling Coalho cheese.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers Comfort Food
programme.desc: Si and Dave cook dishes to feed a multitude - just the thing to impress your guests or to fill up the family. Their salmon pie with spinach and hollandaise is a showstopper and their chocolate and cherry buns make a perfect centrepiece.

programme.title: Kate And Larapinta
programme.desc: Kate Leeming embarks on a 700km solo cycle along Australia's remote Finke River. Battling searing heat, mechanical failures and exhaustion, she confronts physical limits and inner ghosts, turning her epic journey into a meditation on purpose, resilience, and what it takes to keep going.

programme.title: It Takes A Village
programme.desc: This documentary shines a light on a very different way of caring for people living with dementia. Korongee, a new facility in a northern suburb of Hobart, combines the world's best dementia care practices with new and revolutionary ideas. Including a focus on individuals and their life experiences, as the basis for their care. Korongee's guiding philosophy is that a person living with dementia is an individual with a rich and unique personality.
